Signs of the World

Bluetooth

History

The name was proposed in 1997 by Jim Kardach of Intel, after King Harald Bluetooth, the 10th-century Danish king who united the Danish tribes into one kingdom. Kardach picked it as a code name for a technology meant to unite communication protocols. The logo is a bind rune that merges Harald's initials, the Younger Futhark runes Hagall and Bjarkan.

Adoption

The rune appears on phones, headphones and speakers around the world, with 4.7 billion Bluetooth chips shipped each year as of 2021.
